answers.question: is the peer set fairly chosen, and are the peers themselves expensive rather than this being cheap?
answers.answer: Not answerable on fairness — zero peer rows were parsed, so the identity and valuation of the peers cannot be checked from what was given. What can be said: the benchmark P/E average of 128 is itself extremely high, so even if this issue at ~52x looks cheap relative to it, the more likely reading is that the peer set (or market) is expensive rather than this issue being genuinely cheap; a 128x industry average P/E is a valuation red flag, not a bargain benchmark.
